text:
Chief Complaint: The patient reports a weak urine stream, which has been present for about a year. The patient also has a history of diabetes, high blood pressure, and an enlarged prostate, which have been ongoing for two, one, and five years, respectively. The patient expresses concern about the uncertainty surrounding their condition.

Past Medical History: The patient has a history of diabetes, high blood pressure, and an enlarged prostate. They also had a stent put in their heart two years ago.

Family History: The patient's mother has a history of migraines.

Social History: The patient consumes alcohol regularly, smokes a beer or two most evenings, and exercises a couple of times a week. They live with their daughter and work as a delivery driver.

Symptoms: The patient reports a weak urine stream, which is mild in severity and currently present. They also report severe dribbling at the end, but the certainty of this symptom is uncertain. The patient denies experiencing back pain, burning when passing urine, or blood in the urine. They also deny having a fever.

Medications: The patient is currently taking Glycomet (Metformin) 500 mg twice a day, Telmisartan 40 mg once a day, and Tamsulosin 0.4 mg at night for their diabetes, high blood pressure, and enlarged prostate, respectively.

Allergies: The patient reports an allergy to peanuts, which causes their lips to swell, but the severity of the reaction is unknown.

Vital Signs: The patient's blood pressure is 117/70 mmHg, oxygen saturation is 98%, heart rate is 78 bpm, and temperature is 36.8°C.

Physical Examination: The bladder is not palpable in the lower abdomen, and the prostate is smooth and enlarged.

Review of Systems: The patient reports negative urinary symptoms.

Clinical Conditions: The patient has diabetes, high blood pressure, and an enlarged prostate.

Clinical Assessment: The doctor assesses that the enlarged prostate is causing the urinary symptoms.

Procedures and Investigations: The doctor plans to conduct kidney function tests, a pelvic ultrasound, and a prostate-specific antigen (PSA) test to further investigate the urinary symptoms.

Clinical Actions: The doctor advises the patient to limit evening fluids and caffeine, seek urgent care if symptoms worsen, and follow up after the results of the investigations are back.

Follow-up: A follow-up consultation is planned after the results of the investigations are back.

Clinical Uncertainties: The patient could not specify when the dribbling at the end began, which is uncertain. The date of the consultation is also uncertain.
